gaps: Hs-Logic cannot measure deals that carry a final_customer string but have no company association (the 'deals related to nothing' case of Story 2): it scans companies, not deals, and uses final_customer only to EXCUSE companies from orphan status. Live HubSQL probe 2026-10-01 fills it: 116 such deals (160 deals with no company at all). Source: hubspot.py lines 349-410; live-hubsql.

Hs-Logic's numbers are partial by design: 10,000-record cap vs live totals of 13,679 companies (73% covered) and 26,293 contacts (38% covered); paging is in default list order so the uncovered remainder is not a random sample. Any deck figure from slides 26-27 must carry 'partial, capped at 10,000'. Source: hubspot.py lines 320/536; search_crm_objects totals.

No deal-level health at all: no duplicate-deal detection, no pipeline/product-line cardinality check (Image 2 gauge 1, logical problem), no year-metric naming check (gauge 2, business problem). Those remain measured only in the SEALSQ property set (BRIEF 2b).

Duplicate detection is exact-match on normalised name/domain/email only (lowercase + whitespace collapse); no fuzzy matching, no legal-suffix stripping, no cross-entity (SEALSQ / IC'Alps / WISeKey) attribution, so the 226 / 281 clusters are a floor, not a count. Source: hubspot.py _normalize line 297-299.

duplicate_ids under-counts for clusters with more than 10 members (README line 74); the orphan detail is sliced to 150 rows and clusters to 60 in the UI, so screenshots show examples, not the population.

Multi-company contacts (193) are flagged as a violation, but HubSpot natively allows many-to-many contact-company associations; the 'single-company cardinality' rule is a house rule stated only in the docstring, not in any governance document in the three repos.

The orphan rule excludes companies whose name string-matches a deal's final_customer; the number excluded by name match is not reported separately (only the 709 edge-companies via association are). The tool therefore partly accepts the cardinality trap it is supposed to expose.

No automated tests in the repo (no test files, no pytest/vitest config, no CI, no .github directory); verification exists only in commit messages ('Verified token-free', '15 confirmed findings from adversarial review').

No deployment evidence for 'HS-LOGIC serverless query layer on Cloud Run (Sep)' (deck slide 10): the repo has no Cloud Run service definition, no gcloud/cloudbuild file, no CI workflow; the only deployment artefacts are docker-compose for a local host and a Windows-laptop launch.json. The compose comment 'broke the deployed app's /portal route once' proves a deployment happened somewhere but not where.
The 'SQL queries' the Python logic claims to mirror (docstring line 304) are not in the repo; the SQL source of truth for orphan/duplicate rules is unavailable to this session.

Single operator dependency: one author, one day of commits (2026-08-28), one hard-coded user path in .claude/launch.json, one private-app token; no commits since merge; no README owner or runbook beyond 'docker compose up'.

The suppression-list export has no execution evidence (no list id, no screenshot); whether crm.lists.write is granted on the private app is unknown, so the only write path may in practice be the CSV fallback.

Scan timestamp of the slide 26-27 screenshots is not recorded in the images or the deck text (slides 26-27 carry only the title 'CRM Health'); the live FC-deal count has since moved from 1,034 to 1,043.

Portal counts in the Overview tab come from the search API 'total' with -1 fallback; the search API total is used, so the Overview numbers are complete even though the health scans are capped (an inconsistency a reader of the dashboard would not see).
